# Bathroom floor: three options from the supplier

## Option A: porcelain tile, 300 x 600 mm, matt

£42 per m². The matt finish grips well when wet (rated R10). It is hard-wearing and easy to clean, but the grout lines need resealing every couple of years. It is cold underfoot unless we add underfloor heating, which would be about £450 extra for our floor. It needs a level floor, and our subfloor needs about a day of levelling first. The tile has a 25-year manufacturer guarantee; the grout has none.

## Option B: vinyl sheet, 2 m wide roll, stone effect

£28 per m². It is warm and soft underfoot and fully waterproof, so it needs no sealing. The surface grips moderately (rated R9) and can get slippery with soapy water. It scratches and dents under heavy furniture, and a deep cut cannot be repaired, only patched. It goes down in a few hours on our existing floor with a thin levelling coat. The guarantee is 10 years, and only if a fitter installs it.

## Option C: natural slate, 400 x 400 mm, riven

£65 per m². The riven surface has the best grip of the three (rated R11), and it looks good for decades. It needs sealing every year to stop stains and water soaking in, and the uneven surface is hard to clean. It is heavy, so our joists need checking by a builder before we order. Fitting takes two days and costs more per m². There is no guarantee on natural stone, only on the sealant.
